A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CompreCap study. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support comparison, including matching material moved between sections.

before.justification: v1 reports original caption evaluations, fine-grained object VQA results, human assessments, and appendix ablations and failure analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and adds unified caption scores and numerical comparisons of agreement with human ratings.

M1.justification: Section 3.3 adds a weighted aggregation step producing S_unified from the object, attribute, and relation scores. The underlying caption decomposition, object matching, LLM assessment, and pixel-coverage procedures remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same 560-image CompreCap dataset and CompreQA-P/CompreQA-Cap tasks. The additional benchmark descriptions in v3 Appendix B do not establish evaluation on new datasets or task scenarios.

E2.justification: The evaluated LVLMs and comparison methods are retained. BLEU, METEOR, ROUGE-L, CIDEr, CLIPScore, and direct Llama3 scoring in v3 Table 3 already appear in v1's human-agreement analyses. Llama3's overall score also already appears in v1 Table S4.

E3.justification: v3 adds the normalized, weighted S_unified evaluation metric and Pearson, Kendall, and Spearman agreement measures. Existing caption-generation and VQA settings remain substantively unchanged. The newly stated default hyperparameters and human-study procedures document existing experiments rather than establish changed settings.

E4.justification: Table 3 extends the human-agreement analysis with quantitative comparisons involving S_unified, supplementing v1's plots. The resolution, evaluator, parser, corrupted-caption, generation-stability, prompt, and VQA failure analyses are retained, sometimes relocated or renumbered.

E5.justification: v3 first reports Pearson, Kendall, and Spearman correlation statistics and discloses averaging independent human ratings in Appendix F. Both versions retain three repeated evaluations and mean-plus-standard-deviation reporting; no increase in repetitions or new significance testing is established.

E6.justification: Existing component scores, VQA results, and ablation values are retained. Tables 2/S3 add unified scores, including 60.05 for GPT-4o and 58.85 for LLaVA-Next-34B. Table 3 adds correlation results, reporting 0.989/0.927/0.982 for S_unified. Appendix B additionally reports benchmark coverage comparisons.

T1.justification: Section 3.3 newly defines S_unified mathematically through rescaling and weighted aggregation, with stated object/attribute/relation weights of 25%/35%/40%. Earlier score definitions remain unchanged, and neither version supplies theoretical guarantees or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same principal contributions: a directed-scene-graph caption benchmark, structured evaluation, fine-grained VQA, and agreement with human judgments. The added statistics support the existing agreement claim without materially changing its scope.

C2.justification: v3 adds a rationale for weighting attributes and relations more heavily because they are harder to describe. Appendix B also interprets annotation coverage and caption detail relative to Visual Genome. The existing limitation concerning unmeasured caption hallucinations is retained.

D1.justification: v1 reports human results without explaining participant recruitment, group separation, or rating procedures. New Appendix F documents 50 participants, separate 20/10/20 annotation/captioning/rating groups, demographics, 56 images per captioner, and independent scoring of all 6,160 captions. This substantially expands documentation of the central human validation without establishing a new study.

R1.justification: v3 adds six references and a focused benchmark-positioning discussion in Appendix B, including COCO-Stuff, SugarCrepe, and Visual Genome. It emphasizes CompreCap's masks, caption detail, coverage, and evaluation procedure while retaining the earlier positioning against DetailCaps and long-caption datasets.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized grammatical and author-information edits, adds acknowledgments, expands the unified-metric and traditional-metric discussion, and reorganizes several appendix subsections. The overall narrative and most existing prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds correlation Table 3, benchmark-comparison Table S8, unified-score columns, and a unified-score Figure 5. v1 Figures 5 and 6 move to v3 Figures S5 and S1. Most other graphics retain their content and design despite relocation and page reflow.

improvement.justification: The participant and scoring disclosures make the existing human validation substantially easier to assess, while numerical agreement comparisons improve transparency. The net gain is limited by an inconsistency in the new aggregate: Section 3.3's stated weights yield 47.52 for InstructBLIP from Table 2's component scores, whereas Table 2 reports 48.16. The retained component results remain interpretable, but this mismatch weakens reproducibility of the added summary score.
